title: Empire of Pain: The Secret History of the Sackler Dynasty
author: Patrick Radden Keefe
target_audience: Readers interested in modern American history
Those following the opioid epidemic and healthcare crises
Students and professionals in public health, medicine, and law
Readers interested in stories of power, wealth, and corporate misconduct
core_themes: The origins and legacy of the Sackler family fortune
The opioid crisis in the United States
The intersection of medicine, business, and ethics
primary_purpose: To expose and document the secretive history of the Sackler family, their role in the marketing and distribution of OxyContin, and their relationship to the origins and escalation of the opioid crisis, exploring how wealth and influence allowed them to shape public perception and evade responsibility for decades.

structure_format.organization: Chronological, spanning three generations of the Sackler family with deep dives into family history, business practices, and legal controversies
features: Contextualization within broader social and historical events

key_concepts_lessons: The Sackler family built a philanthropic legacy that masked the source of their wealth.
Aggressive pharmaceutical marketing practices contributed significantly to public health crises.
Corporate influence over regulatory and medical institutions can undermine public safety.
Reputation laundering and philanthropy were strategic tools to maintain public esteem.
The opioid epidemic was not a natural disaster, but a result of deliberate business decisions.
Legal systems struggle to hold wealthy and powerful actors accountable.
notable_features: Multi-generational family biography intertwined with social commentary
Clear connections between private decisions and public consequences
Balancing of personal stories with larger systemic issues
cultural_historical_context: Published amid the ongoing fallout from the opioid crisis, at a time of heightened scrutiny over pharmaceutical industry practices and billionaire philanthropy. The book connects the Sackler name—previously prominent in arts and culture—to newfound notoriety as the family behind Purdue Pharma and OxyContin.
reception_impact: Critically acclaimed, finalist for the 2021 Baillie Gifford Prize and other major awards
Praised for its depth of research and compelling storytelling
Contributed to public awareness and debate about corporate responsibility for the opioid epidemic
Some family members and allies have disputed its portrayal; ignited discussions about accountability and philanthropy
Frequently cited in legal, journalistic, and policy discussions about opioids and pharmaceutical regulation
comparable_titles: Dopesick: Dealers, Doctors, and the Drug Company that Addicted America by Beth Macy
Pain Killer: An Empire of Deceit and the Origin of America's Opioid Epidemic by Barry Meier
Bad Blood: Secrets and Lies in a Silicon Valley Startup by John Carreyrou
The Family That Built an Empire of Pain (New Yorker article by Patrick Radden Keefe)
